To draw the isometric view from the given first angle orthographic projections (Figure 1):

1. **Analyze Projections**: From the top view, observe the overall width ($75\text{ mm}$) and length ($100\text{ mm}$ with three $25\text{ mm}$ divisions). From the front view, note the heights and step features ($16\text{ mm}$ heights).
2. **Isometric Axis**: Set up three axes at $120^\circ$ to each other ($30^\circ$ to the horizontal base).
3. **Box Method**: Construct a bounding isometric box of dimensions corresponding to maximum length, width, and height.
4. **Construct Features**: Mark the dimensions $25\text{ mm}$ successively along the length and construct the stepped profile as shown in the front and top orthographic views, ensuring all lines are drawn using isometric scale or actual measurements if standard isometric projection is specified.
proTip: Use true lengths rather than isometric lengths only if instructed to draw an 'isometric projection' instead of an 'isometric view'.
